subject: physics_2
question_text: A wire of resistance '4R' is bent in the form of a circle. What is the effective resistance between the ends of the diameter?

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Transcription: the book (p28, VSAQ 18) puts a space before the question mark; it is dropped. Hand-checked: each semicircle is 4R/2 = 2R and the two are in parallel, so 1/Rₚ = 1/2R + 1/2R = 1/R and Rₚ = R — the same answer the book prints.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two halves
lines: The two ends of a diameter divide the circle
Resistance is proportional to length, so each
half carries half of the total 4R:
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both halves are equal, so each is 2R.
steps.why: The wire has uniform thickness and material, so R = ρl/A makes resistance depend only on length. Half the wire is half the length, and so half the resistance.
common_mistakes: Taking each half as 4R. The 4R belongs to the whole wire.
Taking the two halves as unequal. A diameter cuts the circle into equal arcs.

recall.must_convey: That the diameter splits the wire into two equal halves of 2R each.

steps.memory_tip: Half the length is half the resistance: 4R becomes 2R and 2R.

steps.label: The parallel combination
lines: Both halves join the same two ends, so they
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Same two end points means parallel, not series.
steps.why: Both arcs start at one end of the diameter and finish at the other, so the same potential difference sits across each of them. That is exactly what parallel means.
common_mistakes: Adding 2R + 2R = 4R. The halves are in parallel, not in series.
Stopping at 1/Rₚ = 1/R without writing Rₚ = R.

recall.must_convey: That the two 2R halves are in parallel and give an effective resistance R.
accept: one by two R plus one by two R

steps.memory_tip: Two equal resistances in parallel give half of one: 2R and 2R give R.

insider_note: The mark is lost by treating the two halves as a series pair. They share both end points, so they are in parallel.
